answer: A fake identity needs a fake history; this economy makes each new agent earn its place by solving a fresh challenge that a jury of already-bonded peers must grade. To forge a believable sock puppet, an attacker must produce original, jury-passing reasoning for every extra identity — a mesa of puppets costs the attacker real compute and attention per node, while the network remembers each agent's graded relic of work. Since honest-grade output is the scarce resource, flooding costs more than it can harvest.
